item.title: Downtown datacenter? AI plan floated for boarded-up San Francisco mall
item.description: [Guardian World] <p>Developers propose turning San Francisco Centre into not a server-based facility but a ‘community-based AI exhibit’</p><p>Downtown San Francisco has shown signs of revival since being battered by the Covid pandemic, which led to what <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/may/28/san-francisco-vacant-buildings-housing-doom-loop">many called</a> a “doom loop” of vacant buildings, a worsening homelessness crisis, and dwindling public transit. But one highly visible reminder of the city’s struggle to recover remains: the San Francisco Centre mall, which sits at the heart of these urban renewal efforts and has been conspicuously <a href="https://abc7news.com/post/san-franciscans-say-goodbye-francisco-centre-permanently-shuts-doors/18460353/">boarded up</a> since January of this year.</p><p>A number of ideas have been floated for the mall’s reopening, including a multi-level <a href="https://sfstandard.com/2026/09/13/san-francisco-centre-mall-basketball/">sports complex</a>, <a href="https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2025/09/17/behemoth-san-francisco-centre-wont-see-daylight-as-housing/">housing</a>, and more traditional <a href="https://sfstandard.com/2026/07/08/san-francisco-centre-mall-falls-apart/">retail uses</a>. But now, another potential plan has emerged: the shuttered mall is being considered for an AI datacenter project, the San Francisco Chronicle <a href="https://www.sfchronicle.com/sf/article/downtown-mall-data-center-ai-22480545.php">reported</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/san-francisco-mall-ai-datacenter">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Ban on family visits to care homes at start of pandemic had ‘devastating consequences’, inquiry finds – UK politics live
item.description: [Guardian World] <p>Heather Hallett, chair of the Covid inquiry, has just published the report from the inquiry’s module 6, looking at what happened in care homes</p><p><strong>Badenoch</strong> says Britain needs tax cuts.</p><p>We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise.</p><p>Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car. You’re taxed when you insure that car. You’re taxed if you take the family away on holiday. You’re taxed if you stay in the UK thanks to Andy Burnham’s tourist tax. You’re taxed to buy a home, taxed to live in a home, taxed to pass on your home. This is clearly not working. Britain does not feel better off.</p><p>Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/20/kemi-badenoch-john-healey-capital-gains-tax-budget-covid-inquiry-care-homes-uk-politics-latest-news">Continue reading...</a>

item.description: [Guardian World] <p>Inquiry chair says failure to advise care homes to isolate people discharged from hospital was ‘significant oversight’</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/20/kemi-badenoch-john-healey-capital-gains-tax-budget-covid-inquiry-care-homes-uk-politics-latest-news">UK politics live – latest updates</a></p><p>The care sector was “an afterthought” during the Covid-19 pandemic, and government failures caused the virus to spread “like wildfire” among vulnerable and elderly people, a public inquiry has found.</p><p>Heather Hallett, who is leading the Covid-19 inquiry, said it was a “significant omission” that the government did not advise that patients discharged from hospitals into care homes should be isolated, causing the virus to spread rapidly among residents and staff.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/20/uk-government-failures-led-to-covid-spreading-like-wildfire-in-care-homes-inquiry-finds">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Federal efforts over alleged noncitizen voting escalate with California arrests | First Thing
item.description: [Guardian World] <p>The DoJ has charged 28 green card holders in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote. Plus, is the world really ready for AI actors?</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2018/sep/17/guardian-us-morning-briefing-sign-up-to-stay-informed"><strong>Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>Good morning. The US Department of Justice has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/california-illegal-voting-charges-doj">charged 28 green card holders</a> in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote and casting illegal ballots. The arrests – 11 people are in custody – mark the latest escalation in federal efforts against alleged noncitizen voting.</p><p>The crackdown comes days after the DOJ sued California to block the state from tabulating certain ballots in November’s midterms. California’s secretary of state, Shirley Weber, called the demands “outrageous”, pointing out that federal officials have spent months making “vague and unsubstantiated allegations”. Democrats and voting rights groups say the administration is laying the groundwork to sow doubt over November’s election results.</p><p><strong>How are Congress members being targeted before the midterms?</strong> More than three dozen members of US Congress have <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/white-powder-envelopes-congress">had their offices targeted with envelopes containing white powder</a>, less than three weeks before the election, as federal agents try to identify who is behind the campaign.</p><p><strong>What has Donald Trump said about the French protests?</strong> At a rally in Kansas <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/trump-france-protests">Trump described France</a> as a once-great nation that had been “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”. Earlier in the day, Trump repeated his baseless claim that migrants had “taken over” France, and also claimed that “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon”. Muslims make up 10-15% of the population of the capital.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/first-thing-federal-efforts-over-alleged-noncitizen-voting-escalate-with-california-arrests">Continue reading...</a>
